rv.q: Jonathan Pryce is one of the best reasons to see Miss Saigon.

The story feels more urgent amid renewed refugee tragedies and our consciousness of the sex trade. And the narrative - helped by unusually graceful lyrics by Boublil and Richard Maltby Jr. - almost distract from the generic Euro-pop ballads and anthems that sound like many we've heard before.
Apart from some impressive performances, there's not much else to make Miss Saigon worthwhile.
It is engaging. It is insulting. It is never boring.
